body:
Meta description examples that bring clicks: 20 templates by page type is the resource you open when your Google position is good, but the clicks don't come.

A good meta description doesn't change your ranking. It decides whether the user clicks on your result or the one below it.

Meta description examples that bring clicks: 20 templates by page type

Below you will find meta description examples for service pages, blog posts, product pages and local pages, ready to adapt to your business.

Each template respects the length Google accepts and contains a concrete reason for someone to click, not just a dry description of the content.

What makes a meta description effective

The meta description appears under the title in search results and is often the only argument your page has left before the user picks another result.

Length and truncation in results

Google shows, on average, up to about 155 characters on desktop, sometimes fewer on mobile. Beyond this limit, the text is cut off in the middle of a word, which looks sloppy.

Put the main idea in the first 120 characters. Everything after that is a bonus, not the essential part.

Words that really trigger the click

Verbs that address the reader directly work well: "find out", "compare", "download". Add a specific detail, such as a deadline, a starting price or a geographic area, in place of general wording.

Avoid repeating the title word for word. The meta description complements the title, it doesn't copy it.

The difference between the SEO title and the meta description

The SEO title (the one that appears blue and underlined on the results page) is the first thing read and weighs directly in the relevance Google associates between the page and the query. The meta description doesn't influence ranking in the same way, but it complements the title's promise with a detail that is missing from it.

A simple example: if the title is "Accounting services for sole traders", the meta description doesn't repeat "accounting services for sole traders", but adds the next piece of information, such as the filing deadline for returns or how to get in touch. The two work together, not in parallel.

Meta description examples for service pages

For an SEO optimization page or any other service page, the meta description should say what the client gets and how the collaboration starts.

  1. SEO optimization: "SEO optimization services for businesses in Romania. We audit your site, fix technical errors and build a content plan with clear monthly reports."
  2. Accounting: "Accounting services for sole traders and small limited companies. Complete bookkeeping, returns filed on time and an accountant who answers the phone."
  3. Office cleaning: "Office cleaning on a monthly contract or a one-off visit. Trained team, professional products, schedule adapted to your hours."
  4. Home appliance repairs: "Home appliance repairs at your home, with free diagnosis and original parts. Same-day appointments in Bucharest and Ilfov."
  5. Legal consulting: "Legal consulting for new companies: contracts, GDPR and dealing with the tax authority, explained without hard-to-understand terms."

Notice the pattern: each example says who it is for, what the service concretely does and what the client gets, without promising guaranteed results.

Meta description examples for blog posts

For informational articles, the meta description works as a promise of useful content. The good review examples site shows exactly this pattern: the reader knows beforehand that they will get templates ready to copy.

  • Practical guide: "How to set up automatic backup for WordPress: three methods, from plugin to command line, with steps checked one by one."
  • Comparison article: "Redis or Memcached for caching: the real differences, with cPanel setup examples and the situations where each makes sense."
  • List of examples: "20 meta description examples for services, articles, products and local pages, ready to adapt for your own site."
  • Explainer article: "What crawl budget is and why it matters for a large site: an explanation for a business owner, not an engineer."
  • General case study: "What a site architecture that helps Google find the important pages looks like, with menu and internal link examples."

Each description above says what exactly the article contains (how many examples, how many steps, what comparison), not just its general topic.

Meta description examples for product pages

In the SEO optimization of an online store, the product meta description has a double role: it persuades the click and confirms availability or warranty, two things that influence the buying decision.

  1. Electronics: "15.6 inch laptop, 16 GB RAM, 512 GB SSD. Delivery in 24 hours, 24-month warranty, free returns within 14 days."
  2. Fashion: "Cotton summer dress, sizes XS-XXL. Order now and get your parcel in two working days, free returns."
  3. Home and garden: "Electric lawn mower, 40 liter collection bag. In stock, free delivery on orders over 300 lei."
  4. Cosmetics: "Moisturizing cream with hyaluronic acid for dry skin, 50 ml. Dermatologically tested, paraben-free, fast delivery."
  5. Car accessories: "Car phone holder with wireless charging, compatible with most models. Tool-free installation, 12-month warranty."

Concrete numbers, such as the delivery time or the warranty length, make the difference between a bland description and one that brings the click.

Meta description examples for local and contact pages

For businesses that depend on customers from a specific area, the meta description must contain the name of the town. The basic rules are the same as for local SEO services: relevance to the area, clear opening hours and a quick way to get in touch.

  • Local dental practice: "Dental practice in Cluj-Napoca, with appointments in the same week. Consultation and a transparent treatment plan."
  • Local car service: "Car service in Timișoara for inspections and mechanical repairs. Computer diagnostics and online booking in five minutes."
  • Contact page: "Contact our team for a personalized quote. We reply on the same working day, by phone or form."
  • Local restaurant: "Restaurant with traditional cuisine in the center of Brașov. Online reservations, daily menu and local delivery."
  • Veterinary clinic: "Veterinary clinic in Sibiu, with emergencies taken by phone. Consultations, vaccinations and surgery for pets."

The name of the city is not filler here: it is exactly the term someone searches for alongside the service.

Common mistakes when writing meta descriptions

The same few mistakes appear on most of the sites you audit or manage.

  • A missing meta description, in which case Google picks a snippet from the page on its own, often an unsuitable text.
  • The same meta description copied across dozens of pages, which cancels any click advantage.
  • Text stuffed with repeated keywords, without a single sentence that sounds natural.
  • Promises the page doesn't keep, such as discounts or stock that no longer exist.
  • A meta description longer than the real content offered on the page.
  • Quotation marks, quote signs or special characters not handled correctly, which show up in the result as broken symbols.
  • A meta description written once, when the site launched, and never reviewed after the business changed its offer.

Fixing these mistakes doesn't require advanced technical knowledge, just the time to rewrite each page one by one, with a real description for its content.

How to test a meta description before publishing

Don't publish a meta description just because it fits the character count. Also check how it looks in context, next to the title and the page address.

  • Write the text in an SEO editor, such as Yoast or Rank Math, if you work on WordPress, and watch the preview for desktop and for mobile.
  • Read the text out loud. If it sounds artificial or cramped, cut a word and rephrase the rest.
  • Check whether the meta description answers the question "why would I click this result and not another one on the same results page".
  • Compare the meta description with those of the top three results for the same search. Repeating the same wording doesn't set you apart in any way.

After publishing, note the date you changed the text. If the click-through rate doesn't move in two to three weeks, come back and try another version, don't give up after a single rewrite.

How to check and optimize existing meta descriptions

Before you rewrite anything, find out what already works and what doesn't. The performance report in Google Search Console shows, for each page, how many impressions and clicks it had, and a low click-through rate at a good position is a clear sign of a weak meta description.

Compare pages with similar positions but different click-through rates. The difference comes, in most cases, from the text shown under the title, not from the content itself.

For a quick technical check of the titles and meta descriptions across the whole site, use the GOAI site analyzer, which flags pages with no meta description or with duplicate text.

Rewrite first the pages with high traffic and a low click-through rate. The impact shows there faster than on a rarely visited page.

Keep a simple list, even in a spreadsheet, with the page address, the old meta description and the new one, plus the date of the change. Without this minimum of records, you will never know which version worked better.

Meta descriptions that also come with rich snippets, such as ratings or prices shown directly in the result, gain extra visual space, but the base text still has to be written carefully, because the snippet doesn't replace it.

Conclusion

The twenty examples above are starting points, not texts to copy as they are. Adapt them to your service, product or city, keep the right length and check the results periodically in Search Console.
